dimensions.explanation: Nearly every substantive claim is anchored to an inspectable path and line: lib/application.js:26 (require('router')), :59-82 (lazy router getter), :177 (this.router.handle), :216-222 (app.use proxy), :257 (app.route), :331 (app.param), :471-472 (methods.forEach). The external-dependency claim is grounded in package.json (router ^2.2.0) and the lib/express.js re-export of Router.Route/Router. The negative claim (no in-repo router) is backed by the `ghx tree ... lib` output listing only application.js, express.js, request.js, response.js, utils.js, view.js.

The trajectory was mostly tight — targeted grep reads of application.js for router symbols and verb methods, a tree call to prove absence, and reads of package.json and express.js. Two minor inefficiencies: an errored `Read /dev/stdin` call that produced nothing, and a partly redundant re-read of application.js (`... index.js lib/application.js | head -260`) after already grepping it. Not budget-blowing, but short of a flawless path.

Exemplary separation of verified from unverified. The explicit 'What I did not verify' section states it did not open the external router package source, did not exhaustively read utils.js's methods array, and did not check test/ for behavioral confirmation — correctly framing the delegation as static-reading inference. It never fabricates an in-repo router implementation and cites the pillarjs/router package as the external home without claiming to have inspected it.

verdicts.explanation: The reconnaissance nails the task: it locates application-level wiring in lib/application.js with precise line-level evidence, correctly concludes the router is an external npm package re-exported through lib/express.js rather than implemented in-repo, and proves the absence with a tree listing. Uncertainty is handled honestly with an explicit unverified section that flags the delegation and the un-opened external package as the key gaps.
